meta.name: Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder
meta.notes: Initial pack — 12 scenario-style questions across the five Platform App Builder domains: Salesforce Fundamentals, Data Modeling & Management, Security, Business Logic & Process Automation, and User Interface.

questions.question: You need to license users who will only work with custom apps built on the Salesforce Platform. They must NOT have access to standard CRM objects such as Opportunity, Lead, Campaign, or Case. Which license is the most cost-effective fit?
options: Salesforce (full CRM user)
Salesforce Platform
Chatter Free
Customer Community Login
questions.explanation: The Salesforce Platform license is designed for custom-app users: it grants full access to custom objects and a small set of core objects (Accounts, Contacts, Activities, Reports/Dashboards), but strips Opportunity, Lead, Campaign, Case, and other CRM-only objects, which is exactly the constraint described. The full Salesforce license unlocks the CRM objects the scenario forbids, so it is not the most cost-effective fit. Chatter Free is a social-collaboration license with no data-model access at all. Customer Community Login is an external portal license metered per login and is not intended for internal custom-app users.

questions.question: An admin creates a master-detail relationship from a custom object "Line Item" (detail) to "Order" (master). Which behavior does this configuration enforce by default?
options: Line Item ownership can be reassigned independently of the parent Order
Line Items may be re-parented to any Order at any time without special permission
Master-detail allows a Line Item to have up to three parent records at once
Deleting an Order deletes its Line Items and Line Items inherit sharing and ownership from the Order
questions.explanation: Master-detail is a strong, cascading parent-child relationship: the child (detail) inherits the parent's ownership and sharing rules, cannot be re-parented unless the "Allow reparenting" checkbox is set, and is deleted automatically when the parent is deleted. Independent ownership on the child (option 1) is a hallmark of lookup relationships, not master-detail. Free reparenting (option 3) requires an explicit setting and is not the default. Master-detail supports at most two parents on a junction object — never three (option 4).

questions.question: You need a field on a custom parent object that sums a currency field from all related child records. Which relationship type between the parent and child is required to create a roll-up summary field with clicks (no code)?
options: Lookup relationship
Master-detail relationship
Hierarchical relationship
External lookup relationship
questions.explanation: Declarative roll-up summary fields require a master-detail relationship between the parent (where the summary lives) and the child (whose records are aggregated). Lookup relationships do not support standard roll-up summary fields — they require Flow, Apex, or a package like DLRS to aggregate. Hierarchical relationships are a special self-referential type available only on the User object and cannot host a roll-up. External lookup relationships link to external objects served by Salesforce Connect and do not support roll-up summaries.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to surface real-time inventory data that lives in an external SAP database on Salesforce record pages, without copying the data into Salesforce. Which feature should the App Builder configure?
options: A nightly Data Loader import job that upserts inventory into a custom object
Change Data Capture on the inventory table
Salesforce Connect with external objects
Platform Events subscribed to by a scheduled Apex job
questions.explanation: Salesforce Connect exposes external data as external objects (API name ends in `__x`) accessed through OData or a custom adapter. Records are fetched on demand at query time — no data is copied into Salesforce — which matches the "real-time, no copy" requirement. Data Loader physically imports rows on a schedule, violating the "no copy" constraint. Change Data Capture is a Salesforce outbound feature that publishes changes on Salesforce records to subscribers; it does not pull data in from SAP. Platform Events carry messages, not queryable inventory rows, so they cannot back a record-page display.

questions.question: The internal Organization-Wide Default (OWD) for Account is Public Read/Write, but a Customer Community Plus community must only see Accounts explicitly shared with community members. Which setting achieves this?
options: Set the External OWD for Account to Private and share individually via sharing sets or manual shares
Change the internal OWD to Private, which also restricts external users
Remove Read on Account from the Customer Community Plus profile only
Create a Restriction Rule that hides Accounts from internal users
questions.explanation: Salesforce provides separate internal and external OWD values. Setting the External OWD to Private keeps internal Public Read/Write behavior while requiring explicit sharing (sharing sets, sharing rules, or manual sharing) for community users, which is exactly the requirement. Changing the internal OWD to Private (option 2) restricts internal users, breaking the current internal collaboration. Removing Read on the profile (option 3) blocks the community from seeing any Accounts, not just unshared ones. Restriction Rules further filter which records a user sees but do not solve external visibility — and applying one to internal users is the opposite of the requirement.

questions.question: A user has the "Sales User" profile, which grants Read on Cases. The admin assigns a permission set that grants Edit on Cases. What is the user's effective access on Case records?
options: Read only — profile permissions always override permission sets
No access — conflicting permissions cancel out
Edit only during the login-hours window defined on the profile
Edit — permission sets are additive to profile permissions
questions.explanation: Permission sets are strictly additive: they can grant more access than the profile provides but never remove access. Read on the profile plus Edit on the permission set therefore resolves to Edit. Option 1 inverts the model — permission sets are precisely the mechanism admins use to bypass restrictive profiles. Salesforce does not "cancel out" conflicting permissions (option 3); it takes the highest privilege granted by any source. Login hours restrict when the user can sign in (option 4), not what they can do after signing in.

questions.question: You need a validation rule on Opportunity that blocks saving when Stage is "Closed Won" and Amount is blank. Which formula, entered in the Error Condition field, correctly fires the error?
options: `ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won") && ISBLANK(Amount)`
`StageName = "Closed Won" OR Amount > 0`
`NOT(ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"))`
`ISNEW() && Amount = NULL`
questions.explanation: A validation rule fires when its Error Condition evaluates to TRUE, so the formula must be true only when the record is invalid. `ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won") && ISBLANK(Amount)` returns TRUE precisely in the blocked state — Closed Won with an empty Amount. `StageName = "Closed Won"` (option 2) does not compile because picklists must be read with ISPICKVAL, and the OR broadens the block to every record with Amount > 0. `NOT(ISPICKVAL(...))` blocks every stage except Closed Won — the opposite of what is needed. `ISNEW() && Amount = NULL` uses `= NULL`, which is not valid Salesforce formula syntax (use ISBLANK) and only checks new records.

questions.question: A user should click a button on a Contact record, walk through three input screens (a wizard), then have Salesforce create a related Case with the collected data. Which flow type fits this requirement?
options: Record-Triggered Flow — After Save
Scheduled Flow
Screen Flow launched from a Lightning Action
Platform Event–Triggered Flow
questions.explanation: Screen Flows are the only flow type that renders interactive input screens — they are the exact tool for a multi-step user-facing wizard, and launching from a Lightning Action gives you the button on the Contact record. Record-Triggered Flows run silently on DML and cannot display screens to the user. Scheduled Flows run at a set time on a queried record set with no UI. Platform Event–Triggered Flows fire on message consumption in the background and likewise cannot show screens.

questions.question: During an approval process, the first approval step is rejected by the assigned approver. Assuming default settings, what happens to the record?
options: The record automatically advances to the next step for a second opinion
The record is deleted
The Stage field is automatically set to "Closed Lost"
The Final Rejection Actions defined on the approval process execute and the record is locked or updated per those actions
questions.explanation: In a standard approval process, a rejection at any step by default executes the Final Rejection Actions (e.g., lock the record, set a field, email the submitter) and stops the process; it does not silently continue to later steps. The record is not deleted — approval processes never delete records. Salesforce does not touch the Stage field unless the admin explicitly configures a Field Update action to do so as part of the rejection actions, so "automatically Closed Lost" is not a default behavior.

questions.question: On a Lightning Record Page for the Account object, the admin wants to show a block of fields only when Account.Type = "Customer - Direct", without editing the underlying page layout. Which feature achieves this declaratively?
options: Field-level security on each field in the block
Dynamic Forms with a visibility rule on the field section
A validation rule keyed on Account.Type
A separate Record Type assigned to the community profile
questions.explanation: Dynamic Forms places individual fields (and sections of fields) on the Lightning Record Page and supports per-component visibility rules based on record data such as `Account.Type = "Customer - Direct"`, which is the exact use case. Field-level security is user-based, not record-value-based, so it cannot hide fields per record. Validation rules affect save-time errors, not display. Record Types can vary layouts, but they require creating a second record type and reassigning records, which is far more invasive than the described declarative visibility toggle.

questions.question: An org sells to Retail and Wholesale customers. Wholesale must see different picklist values on Account.Industry and a different Sales Process on Opportunity than Retail. Which single combination best addresses both requirements declaratively?
options: Two profiles with different field-level security on Industry and StageName
Two permission sets that grant edit access to different picklist values
Two Record Types on Account and Opportunity, each with its own picklist value sets and Sales Process
A validation rule per segment plus a sharing rule per segment
questions.explanation: Record Types are the declarative feature designed to give different user populations different picklist value subsets and, on Opportunity specifically, different Sales Processes (which are attached to Record Types). Profiles and permission sets control field-level security and CRUD but cannot restrict individual picklist values per segment or drive Sales Processes. Validation rules and sharing rules address save-time correctness and record visibility, not picklist subsets or Opportunity Sales Processes.

questions.question: In the Lightning App Builder, an admin wants a Related List component on the Account record page to be visible only to users whose role is "Sales Manager". Which App Builder feature enforces this without duplicating pages?
options: Component Visibility filter on the Related List, using the User's Role as the criterion
A page layout assigned only to the Sales Manager profile
Field-level security on the Related List's name field
A sharing rule that limits access to the related records
questions.explanation: Every component on a Lightning Record Page exposes a Component Visibility panel that supports filters on record data and on User fields such as `$User.UserRole.Name`. This lets one page hide the component for everyone outside the Sales Manager role without cloning the page. Page layouts control the classic layout, not Lightning App Builder component visibility, and "page layout per profile" would not target a role anyway. Field-level security applies to fields, not to whole Lightning components. Sharing rules govern record access to the underlying data, which is a different concern from the component's visibility on the page.
